Works
Out-of-water, hardstand

The brief

Hauled out for shaft seal failure — and a full once-over

This Technomarine 84 came out of the water with a failed PSS dripless shaft seal — a split in the bellows was letting water gush through into the bilge — with corrosion built up inside the coupling flange behind it. With the vessel already up on the hardstand, we used the haul-out to work through the running gear, hull and topsides properly rather than just chasing the leak.

Scope of works

What we did

Replaced the failed PSS dripless shaft seals

Full service of the main engines, gearboxes & generators

Multiple fibreglass hull repairs

Trim tab repairs

Swim platform repairs

Propspeed applied to props, shafts, rudders, skegs & trim tabs

Full antifoul application

Anode replacement across the running gear and hull

On the hardstand

Out-of-water, start to finish

The failed seal

The failed seal — water was gushing through a split in the bellows the owner had temporarily repaired with duct tape

Corrosion inside the coupling flange, exposed once we disconnected the shaft from the gearbox

New PSS shaft seal fitted, fresh clamps and bellows

Fibreglass, running gear & finish

Fairing a topsides repair, masked off ready to fair back

Twin shafts, skegs & props stripped back for service

Hull primed and painted, Propspeed applied, ready for launch
